summary: Okanogan County, WA 40-foot L-4 lookout built 1933, gone by 1958; a 2021 visit reported four concrete footings left after the 2014 Carlton Complex fire.

facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1958 per the sources (FFLOS says removed; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed). A visit reported in April 2021 found four concrete footings.

visit.drive_up: About 6.5 miles up NF-41 from near the Loup to Forest Road 250, then about 2 miles east and south on foot
visit.trail_note: Mostly easy walk on the forest road; the last 100 feet or so to the summit need some bushwhacking through deadfall and brush

corrections.why: FFLOS and Firelookout.com both describe a 40-foot tower, about 12.2 m. No source read gives 4.3 m as the tower height.

events.note: Ted Healam listed as lookout in 1932, a year before the tower was built (WillhiteWeb; the 2021 visit cites a Methow Grist mention)
40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built on the summit
Panorama photographs taken from the site
Tower destroyed in 1958 per Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; FFLOS says removed in 1958
Carlton Complex Fire burned the forest from Finley Canyon to Thrapp; the 2021 visit says lookout artifacts remained on the summit until the 2014 fires
Registered October 17, 2010; nominated by Irene Potter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says removed in 1958; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1958; the 2021 visit says destroyed sometime in 1958. Dates agree; the manner differs. Recorded as destroyed in 1958.

FFLOS (undated) says considerable ruins can still be found; Firelookout.com says they all burned in the 2010s; the April 2021 visit found four concrete footings. The most recent first-hand description is the 2021 visit; footings are recorded.
WillhiteWeb and the 2021 visit place lookout Ted Healam in 1932, a year before the 1933 tower. Both recorded; possibly an earlier lookout or a different structure.
FFLOS lists Washington State Schools as administrator. Current ownership and public access are not stated in the sources read.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 4.3 corrected to 12.2 (40 ft per FFLOS and Firelookout.com). Recent first-hand description is one personal blog (April 2021); WillhiteWeb is a personal site. Land status and public access not verified; the brief access 'unknown' is kept. The 1932 Healam date predates the 1933 build per the same sources and is recorded, not reconciled. Brief agency (Washington State Schools) follows FFLOS only.
